incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered: hartwell-prod-reserved-pool-high-latency (sev2) — 95th latency > 2.5s for 10m. Link: https://pd.example/alerts/ABC123

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident #INC-2026-549 acknowledged by Devon

Devon: Acked. I'm oncall. Seeing customer-facing errors in logs? Sara, are they reporting?

Sara: Yes — Hartwell reported slow inference and timeouts from their integration tests ~10:05 UTC. They're seeing 5xxs and long tails.

Annie: Looking at console — reserved pool utilization at 98%, queued requests rising. KV cache evictions spike at 10:02.

Matt: Runtime metrics: model-worker pods on reserved nodes spiking CPU and GPU mem pinned. Autoscaler didn't add nodes — requests queued instead. I see kube events for quota denial.

Devon: Steps: (1) scale reserved pool for tenant hartwell manually, (2) enable burst-capacity, (3) open temporary routing to fallback region. Annie, can you run the scale command?

Annie: Running: ```redwood-admin scale --tenant hartwell --pool reserved --delta 3 --reason "emergency scale for latency spike"```

Ops-Bot: Command accepted. Provisioning 3 GPU nodes (g5.16x) for hartwell-reserved-pool. ETA ~3m.

Annie: Nodes are booting. Kube shows new nodes joining, pods scheduling. Eviction rate dropping.

Matt: Patching runtime to use degraded model variant for non-critical inference to reduce mem pressure: ```kubectl -n redwood patch configmap hartwell-runtime -p '{"data":{"model_variant":"quant-8b-fast"}}'``` Rolling update initiated.

Devon: Good. While that's rolling, I'm going to open a temporary route to hosted fallback for <1% of traffic to reduce peak. Doing a canary reroute.

Annie: Queue length decreasing, 95th latency down from 2.7s -> 1.4s as nodes come up. KV cache miss rate still high but dropping.

Sara: Hartwell confirms improvement on their side — success rate back to normal for most requests, some retries required. They want a summary and ETA for RCA.

Devon: Marking incident as mitigated. I'll hold the pager and monitor for 30m. Can someone take notes for postmortem? Matt, can you capture the autoscaler behavior? Annie, note cache eviction pattern and quota denial.

Matt: Noted — autoscaler didn't trigger due to a quota check: cloud provider returned InsufficientInstanceCapacity for g5-ish region, so the autoscaler rejected scale. Manual scale used a different instance type which succeeded. Will dump: ```kubectl get events --namespace reserved-pools | tail -n 50``` and share in postmortem.

Annie: Cache note: sudden KVCache thrash due to a tenant-side burst of long-context requests which caused high memory pressure; eviction TTLs were aggressive. Suggest we add an alert on KV eviction rate crossing 5%/min.

Devon: Agreed. Actions: 1) Postmortem draft with timeline and root cause (tenant burst + provider IPC + autoscaler gating) 2) Add KV eviction alert 3) Improve autoscaler fallback path to try alternate instance types before failing 4) Customer comms to Hartwell summarizing mitigation and next steps.

Sara: I'll send Hartwell a concise incident summary and ask if they can share request patterns that triggered burst.

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident #INC-2026-549 status: mitigated -> awaiting postmortem.

Devon: I'll hand this off to the next oncall in 20m. If anything flares up ping me directly. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Ops-Bot: Monitoring window started for 30m. If latency rises >1s above baseline will repage.

Annie: Adding follow-ups to backlog: AUTOSCALER-342 (fallback instance types), KVCACHE-121 (alert & TTL tuning), DOCS-77 (runbook update for manual scale), COMM-89 (customer note template).

Devon: Closing thread for now. Postmortem owner: Matt. Communication lead: Sara.

Matt: Will own postmortem. Drafting timeline now.

Sara: Customer note sent, awaiting reply.

Devon: Last check: 95th latency steady at 1.2s for 10m. Closing pager. Good job team. :white_check_mark:
